title: A filtered colimit of henselian pairs is henselian
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a directed set (a nonempty preordered set in which any two elements have a common upper bound, Stacks Categories Definition Tag 00D3) and $(A_\lambda,I_\lambda)_{\lambda\in\Lambda}$ a directed system of pairs: commutative rings $A_\lambda$ with ideals $I_\lambda$ and ring maps $\varphi_{\mu\lambda}:A_\mu\to A_\lambda$ for $\mu\le\lambda$ ($\varphi_{\lambda\lambda}=\mathrm{id}$, $\varphi_{\lambda\nu}\circ\varphi_{\mu\lambda}=\varphi_{\mu\nu}$) with $\varphi_{\mu\lambda}(I_\mu)\subseteq I_\lambda$. Assume every pair $(A_\lambda,I_\lambda)$ is henselian [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]. Let $A=\varinjlim_\lambda A_\lambda$ be the colimit of commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], with coprojections $\alpha_\lambda:A_\lambda\to A$, and $I=\bigcup_\lambda\alpha_\lambda(I_\lambda)$. Then $I$ is an ideal of $A$ contained in the Jacobson radical of $A$, and $(A,I)$ is a henselian pair.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0FWT (lemma-filtered-colimits-henselian, line 2885) and its proof (radical: $u\in1+I$ comes from $u_\lambda\in1+I_\lambda$, a unit by Algebra Lemma lemma-contained-in-radical; henselian: Stacks' Definition Tag 09XE (definition-henselian-pair, lifting of coprime monic factorizations), descending $f,g_0,h_0,g_0',h_0'$ to a stage). Stacks' definition is the factorization form 09XE while [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology] is the idempotent form (09XI (3)), so the split of this node either passes through Lemma Tag 09XI (lemma-characterize-henselian-pair) or proves the idempotent form directly; Example Tag 0FWU (example-moret-bailly) shows filteredness is needed

proof.text: *Each stage satisfies the factorization criterion.* Since $(A_\lambda,I_\lambda)$ is henselian [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], [lem-weil-pbc-henselian-factorization-criterion] ($\Rightarrow$) gives for every $\lambda$: (i$_\lambda$) $I_\lambda$ is contained in the Jacobson radical of $A_\lambda$; (ii$_\lambda$) for every monic $F\in A_\lambda[T]$ and every factorization $\overline F=G_0H_0$ in $(A_\lambda/I_\lambda)[T]$ into monic polynomials generating the unit ideal there are monic $G,H\in A_\lambda[T]$ with $F=GH$ reducing to $G_0,H_0$ modulo $I_\lambda$.

proof.text: *$I$ lies in the Jacobson radical of $A$.* Let $u\in1+I$, $u=1+\alpha_\lambda(x)$ with $x\in I_\lambda$ (definition of $I$). By (i$_\lambda$) of step 2 and [lem-weil-pbc-jacobson-radical-one-plus-units] ($\Rightarrow$) for $(A_\lambda,I_\lambda)$, $u_\lambda=1+x$ is a unit of $A_\lambda$, say $u_\lambda v=1$; then $u=\alpha_\lambda(u_\lambda)$ and $u\,\alpha_\lambda(v)=\alpha_\lambda(1)=1$, so $u$ is a unit of $A$. As $I$ is an ideal (step 1 (c)) and every element of $1+I$ is a unit, [lem-weil-pbc-jacobson-radical-one-plus-units] ($\Leftarrow$) gives $I\subseteq\operatorname{rad}(A)$. This is the first assertion of the statement, and condition (i) of [lem-weil-pbc-henselian-factorization-criterion] for $(A,I)$.

proof.text:
*Descending a coprime monic factorization to a stage.* Let $f\in A[T]$ be monic of degree $n$ and $\overline f=g_0h_0$ with $g_0,h_0\in(A/I)[T]$ monic generating the unit ideal; write $1=g_0g_0'+h_0h_0'$ with $g_0',h_0'\in(A/I)[T]$. If $A/I=0$, then $1\in I\subseteq\operatorname{rad}(A)$ by step 3, so $A$ has no maximal ideal and $A=0$ (a nonzero ring has a maximal ideal); then $g=h=f$ satisfy $f=gh$ in the zero ring $A[T]$, are monic, and reduce to $g_0,h_0$ in the zero ring $(A/I)[T]$; so assume $A/I
eq0$ (hence $A
eq0$). Write $f=T^n+\sum_{k<n}a_kT^k$, $g_0=T^r+\sum_{k<r}c_kT^k$, $h_0=T^s+\sum_{k<s}d_kT^k$, and choose preimages in $A$ of the $c_k$, $d_k$ and of the coefficients of $g_0',h_0'$. By step 1 (a) all these finitely many elements of $A$, together with the $a_k$, are images under $\alpha_\lambda$ of elements of one $A_\lambda$. This gives $F=T^n+\sum_{k<n}b_kT^k\in A_\lambda[T]$ with $\alpha_\lambda(F)=f$, monic $G\in A_\lambda[T]$ of degree $r$ and $H$ of degree $s$, and $G',H'\in A_\lambda[T]$, such that the reductions modulo $I$ of $\alpha_\lambda(G),\alpha_\lambda(H),\alpha_\lambda(G'),\alpha_\lambda(H')$ are $g_0,h_0,g_0',h_0'$. proof.text: *Conclusion.* By steps 3 and 5, $(A,I)$ satisfies (i) and (ii) of [lem-weil-pbc-henselian-factorization-criterion], so by its direction ($\Leftarrow$) $(A,I)$ is henselian [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]; with step 1 (c) ($I$ is an ideal) and step 3 ($I\subseteq\operatorname{rad}(A)$) this proves the statement.

split_report.summary: Route (a). Read Stacks 0FWT and its proof (more-algebra.tex l.2885), 09XE, 09XI, 0AME (algebra.tex l.3555), 00D3 (directed sets are nonempty); tags verified in stacks-project/tags/tags. The DAG's henselian is the idempotent form, so the proof passes through the reviewed lem-weil-pbc-henselian-factorization-criterion ((A,I) henselian iff (i) I in rad and (ii) coprime monic factorizations lift) in both directions. Six steps: (1) elementwise facts from the reviewed leaves filtered-colimit-algebras-elementwise (R = Z) and filtered-colimit-rings-zero, I is an ideal, x with alpha(x) in I lands in some I_nu, induced maps mod I; (2) the criterion at each stage; (3) 1+I consists of units, so I in rad(A), via the new Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-jacobson-radical-one-plus-units (Stacks 0AME, Ideal.mem_jacobson_bot); (4) descent of f, g0, h0, g0', h0' to a stage nu with monic lifts and the relations holding mod I_nu (Stacks' one sentence written out; the case A/I = 0 handled: then A = 0); (5) lift at nu by (ii_nu) and push to A; (6) the criterion backwards. Statement: 'directed set' made explicit as nonempty (Stacks 00D3; for empty Lambda the union I would be empty, not an ideal). No Lean candidate in slopmaster2.

lean.statement: theorem filteredColimit_henselianPair {Λ : Type u} [Preorder Λ] [IsDirected Λ (· ≤ ·)] [Nonempty Λ] (F : Λ ⥤ CommRingCat.{u}) [HasColimit F] (J : ∀ i : Λ, Ideal (F.obj i)) (hJ : ∀ {i j : Λ} (f : i ⟶ j), Ideal.map (F.map f).hom (J i) ≤ J j) (hH : ∀ i : Λ, HenselianRing (F.obj i) (J i)) : ∃ I : Ideal (colimit F : CommRingCat.{u}), (I : Set (colimit F : CommRingCat.{u})) = {x | ∃ (i : Λ) (a : F.obj i), (colimit.ι F i).hom a = x ∧ a ∈ J i} ∧ I ≤ Ideal.jacobson ⊥ ∧ HenselianRing (colimit F : CommRingCat.{u}) I
